title: CDEPE volunteer teachers’ indefinite strike call over unpaid stipends and public-service hiring terms
location: Brazzaville (the declaration was made public there); actual strike locations are not reported.
organizer: Coordination des diplômés des écoles professionnelles de l’enseignement (CDEPE)
threshold_50_evidence: Not established. The ADIAC report says the CDEPE called volunteer teachers to observe an indefinite strike and mentions eleven departmental bureaus and its base. It does not report the number who actually stopped work, an in-person public gathering, or strike attendance. The 4,660 teachers assigned under the 2018 protocol are historical staffing context, not turnout.

title.summary: The reports identify the CDEPE and describe an indefinite strike over non-compliance with its government agreement and hiring terms.

start_date.summary: The Feb. 1 reports state that the strike began Monday, Jan. 31.

end_date.summary: No end date or later strike status is reported in these source extracts.

location.summary: The declaration was made public in Brazzaville; the actual sites of any work stoppage or public gathering are not specified.

scope.summary: The declaration addressed eleven departmental bureaus and called volunteer teachers broadly; actual geographic implementation is unverified.

organizer.summary: The Coordination des diplômés des écoles professionnelles de l’enseignement (CDEPE) is named as issuing the declaration.

demands.summary: The report attributes the action to unpaid scholarship arrears and grievances over the government agreement and seniority in hiring into the public service; provisional map to labor_wage_dispute.

participants_original.summary: No protester or work-stoppage attendance estimate is given.

participants_min.summary: No minimum attendance is reported; eleven bureaus and 4,660 teachers assigned in 2018 are not strike turnout.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The report confirms a strike call/claimed onset but not a qualifying public gathering or 50 participants; 4,660 is historical staffing context, not turnout.

protester_violence.summary: The captured text does not describe event conduct or protester violence.

state_response.summary: The captured reports do not describe event-specific government response; all seven dimensions remain unknown.

eligibility.summary: A government-targeted teacher labor action is reported, but the evidence does not establish that it became a qualifying public gathering or reached 50 participants; keep pending evidence.

notes: The article date is Feb. 1, but its stated action start is Jan. 31, so the candidate is retained in this January unit. S001, S002, and S008 are same-story variants within the ADIAC reporting origin, not three independent confirmations. S001’s exact PDF URL returned only “not accessible via this tool” on web.open; no HTTP status or publisher denial was observed, and its search_only status is retained. No official approval or baseline comparison is implied.
open_questions: Did volunteer teachers actually stop work on Jan. 31, and at which sites?
Was there a public, in-person protest action and did at least 50 people participate?
How many schools/teachers observed the strike, if any?
When did the action physically end or resume?
Did the government respond specifically to this action?
Does the official baseline or supplementary procedure alter the provisional mapping?
